18.75% (Quad) |modifiers = [[Mutation]] (Hard only) |music-1 = [[File:(Official) Tower Defense Simulator OST - The Hunt|250px|center|thumb]] }} __TOC__ ==Description== '''Huevous Hunt''' was the event [[Maps|map]] for [[The Hunt Event]]. Like other event maps, this map had a specialized wave structure with special enemies. Players started with a varying amount of cash, based on how many players there were in the match and the difficulty chosen. Uniquely, to play with other players, a party needed to be created. Upon triumphing, players were rewarded with the [[Quests#After The Hunt|After The Hunt]] in easy mode while the {{RLinkC|16736381810|Scout Egg}} was in stock, while in hard mode it gives the {{Color|Korblox|Korblox}} [[Warden]] skin. This map had the [[Mutation]] modifier, which increased enemy health by 10% every wave after they have debuted. As the [[Mutation]] modifier was not applied at the beginning but instead when the first wave started, it did not boost the rewards. The health was also set to 100 on both Beginner and Hard, despite there being no [[HP Locked]] modifier. You only got cash from them if they were killed in this map, or in some cases, damaged by a specific amount of health. Additionally, the amount gotten was a set amount of cash, which was not always equal to the enemy's health. In solo, you receive 100% of the cash when an enemy was killed or damaged enough. With each additional player, this decreased by 25%, which meant that in a quad, you only got 25% of the cash. This amount is distributed between players based on how much damage they dealt. However, if a player did not deal any damage, they would receive a percentage of the enemy's full cash upon its death or when it was damaged enough, which was 12.5% in duo, 16.7% in trio and 18.75% in quad. If it was a decimal, it was rounded up. For example, the [[Korblox Seeker (The Hunt)|Korblox Seeker]] gave {{Money|20}} when killed in solo, {{Money|15}} in duo, {{Money|10}} in trio and {{Money|5}} in quad between the players that damaged it. Players that did not damage it received {{Money|2.5}} in duo, which was rounded up to {{Money|3}}, {{Money|3.34}} in trio, which was rounded down to {{Money|3}} {{Money|3.75}} in quad, which was rounded up to {{Money|4}}. ==Design & Path== '''Huevous Hunt''' took place on a desert surrounded by a few grassy areas and mountains, separated by a giant river. Multiple cactuses and trees were scattered across the map. On the map there were multiple black roads with yellow lines and grey sidewalk. There were two bridges on this map, one large red bridge connecting two hills and a smaller brown bridge. There was a yellow house with a red roof and blue floor on this map. There was also a white lighthouse with black stripes. As the waves progressed, the map slowly became corrupted by the Korblox forces, starting from the portal. The corruption was destroyed upon triumphing, though the map got fully corrupted upon loss. The ground turned purple and black. Trees and cactuses turned into translucent blue dead trees. A few objects started floating in the air. Additionally, the skybox also gets corrupted with waves. ==Interactive Map== {{Map:HuevousHunt}} ==Story== [[T.D.S. Organization]] dispatches agents lead by the [[Commander (Narrator)|Commander]] to investigate a new threat that has emerged in '''Huevous Hunt'''. This turns out to be the Korblox Empire, which has began their invasion on the place, slowly corrupting it. The battle ends with the [[Korblox Deathwalker (The Hunt: Mega Edition)|Korblox Deathwalker]] being defeated, stopping the Korblox Empire for the time being. ==Rewards== The game calculated how many {{Coins|Coins}} and {{Exp|}} you receive based on how many waves you survived and if you won a match. During periods of 100% more {{Exp|}} (Friday – Sunday), any {{Exp|}} earned was multiplied by 2x through the [[XP Boost]] modifier. The VIP [[Gamepasses|gamepass]] also multiplied any {{Exp|}} earned by 1.25x through the [[VIP Boost]] modifier. Any rewards that ended in a decimal point were rounded down, no matter the first figure of the leading decimal. Rewards were calculated as: {| class="tds-table pad-10" style="text-align: center; margin:1em auto" !Coins Reward !EXP Reward |- ! colspan="2" |Easy Rewards |- |{{Coins|80}} ÷ (1 + [(10 ÷ Current Wave) - 1]^1.3) + {{Coins|100}} (Triumph Only) |{{Exp|25}} ÷ (1 + [(10 ÷ Current Wave) - 1]) |- ! colspan="2" |Hard Rewards |- |{{Coins|200}} ÷ (1 + [(15 ÷ Current Wave) - 1]^1.3) + {{Coins|100}} (Triumph Only) |{{Exp|80}} ÷ (1 + [(15 ÷ Current Wave) - 1]) |} ===Badges=== There were also a few [[badges]] which could be obtained when playing this map, which may have had additional rewards alongside the [[Badges|badge]]. These were: {{Badge |title = Defeat Deathwalker! {{!}} The Hunt First Edition |description = This badge was earned by completing Tower Defense Simulator's Gamemode for The Hunt: First Edition. |image = THBadge1.png |obtainable = No }} {{Badge |title = Eggs?!? |description = Eggs. |image = THBadge2.png |obtainable = No }} ==Wave Structure== The formula for calculating wave bonus on each wave in easy was: :{{Money|450}} + Waves Completed × {{Money|1,350}} In hard mode, it was instead calculated as: :({{Money|675}} - ((Players - 1) * 75)) + Waves Completed × ({{Money|1,125}} - ((Players - 1) * 125)) There is no wave clear bonus on this map. The waves in '''Huevous Hunt''' could not be skipped. They followed these timings: {| class="wikitable align-center" style="width:50%; margin: 0 auto;" ! rowspan="2" |Waves ! colspan="2" |Wave Timer |- !Beginner !Hard |- |1-2 |1:00 |1:00 |- |3 |1:10 |1:00 |- |1-2 |1:00 |1:00 |- |3 |1:10 |1:00 |- |4 |1:15 |1:00 |- |5-9 |1:20 |1:00 |- |10 |∞ |1:00 |- |11-12 | - |1:00 |- |13-14 | - |1:10 |- |15 | - |∞ |} '''Bolded''' names indicates an enemy type's debut. ----

==Strategy== ===Beginner Mode=== *In beginner, the match starts with a preset loadout, with the towers being the [[Minigunner]], [[Soldier]], [[Trapper]], [[Pyromancer]] and [[Warden]]. **Additionally, these towers use their default skin and the golden perk cannot be applied. *Early on, the [[Soldier]] and [[Pyromancer]] can be quite effective at clearing out hordes of weaker enemies. **At later waves, multiple enemies gain burn immunity, though the [[Pyromancer]] can still fare well against them. ***Other towers like the [[Minigunner]] or [[Soldier]] can still be useful at helping the [[Pyromancer]] clear out these enemies. *Due to its high DPS, the [[Minigunner]] is the best choice for later waves. *The [[Warden]] can be useful at stunning enemies, though it is not necessary. **On later waves, some enemies spawn with the stun immunity, making the [[Warden]] only slow them down instead of stunning them. ===Hard Mode=== *Early on, towers like the [[Pyromancer]] or [[Shotgunner]] can be quite effective at clearing out hordes of enemies. **Do note that later on, multiple enemies gain burn immunity on specific waves while the [[Korblox Undead (The Hunt)|Korblox Undead]] always have it. It is recommended to bring other towers alongside the [[Pyromancer]], such as the [[Soldier]], [[Ace Pilot]] or [[Shotgunner]]. *Towers like the [[Minigunner]], [[Pursuit]] or [[Accelerator]] can be quite effective later on at clearing out the hordes of enemies. **Towers with both hidden detection and lead detection, like the [[Minigunner]] or [[Accelerator]] can be especially useful due to the high amounts of these enemies that appear. *The [[Commander]] and [[DJ Booth]] can be quite useful at boosting the firerate and range of towers respectively. *Do note that the map does not have any cliff spaces, making cliff tower useless. ==Gallery== {{Gallery| {{GalleryHeader|Thumbnails}} TheHuntThumbnail.png|'''Huevous Hunt''' on the game thumbnail. }} ==Trivia== *'''Huevous Hunt''' appears to have been based on the fifth Roblox starter place, though remade in a more blocky style. *The car that appeared on this map was actually driveable. **Additionally, when the map was corrupted if you were in the car, you would levitate up into the air along with the car. **The car also happened to be part of the fifth Roblox starter place, both being drivable. *There were five eggs on this map which when collected, grant the ''Eggs?!?'' badge, all of which are from the [[w:c:Roblox:Roblox Easter Egg Hunt 2013|2013 Egg Hunt]]. These eggs are: **{{RLinkC|102607079|Builderman Egg}}, which could be found at the top of the brown hill. **{{RLinkC|102618069|Royal Fabergé Egg}}, which could be found inside of the cave in the brown hill. **{{RLinkC|102614621|Dreamweaver Fabergé Egg}}, which could be found next to the grey road on the brown hill. **{{RLinkC|110705572|Outrageous Egg}}, which could be found near the brown mountain around the red bridge. **{{RLinkC|110705006|Regal Dragon Fabergé Egg}}, which could be found in the corner next to the bridge. *The enemies that appeared on this map are based on the [[w:c:Roblox:Korblox's Empire|Korblox's Empire]], a medieval fantasy group, one of the few groups which had multiple accessories, gears and packages made for it. **The [[Redcliff Traitor (The Hunt)|Redcliff Traitor]] is partially based on the [[w:c:Roblox:Knights of RedCliff|Knights of RedCliff]], which is also a group which had multiple accessories and gears made for it. ***The [[Redcliff Traitor (The Hunt)|Redcliff Traitor]] is considered a traitor as the [[w:c:Roblox:Korblox's Empire|Korblox]] and [[w:c:Roblox:Knights of RedCliff|RedCliff]] are sworn enemies. *The word "''Huevous''" is similar to the word "''Huevo''" which means "''Egg''" in Spanish. *This is the first and currently the only map that did not have any cliff spaces. *The music that played on this map is a remix of [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=S-XBFN6LR0Y The Great Strategy]. ==Update History== *'''15 March 2024''' - [[v1.16.0]] **'''Huevous Hunt''' added. **{{Bug}} [[Commander (Narrator)|Commander]]'s first dialogue animation on Wave 4 in Beginner does not play. *'''30 March 2024''' - [[v1.17.0]]a **'''Huevous Hunt''' removed. {{MapNavBox}}
